answer: The ember report shows the merge explicitly at each lantern. Each collapsed cluster gets one cedar weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, an farming party who spins up 85 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 184 times the capital for one share. A farm of 1677 identities would post 1077 proofs and burn roughly 49 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
